title: Preflight CI for Private IaC: lint, policy-run, plan annotations and health prechecks
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Add a robust pre-merge and pre-apply CI pipeline for Private (VPC) Terraform modules that runs formatting/linting, policy-as-code (Conftest/OPA), unit plan validation, and quick health prechecks against a staging VPC. Goal is to block unsafe or non-compliant changes early and provide actionable plan annotations to engineers.
background: We currently rely on ad-hoc developer checks and manual reviews for Private deployment IaC. Incidents during upgrades (drift, mis-configured security groups, KMS mismatches) are costly and slow. Other teams have spike pipelines but there is no standardized preflight for module maintainers and PR reviewers. This ticket bundles the CI pattern, failure modes, and integration points with our repo management (GitHub) and orchestration layer (Atlantis/Spacelift evaluated).
proposed_solution: 1) Implement GitHub Actions job template that runs: terraform fmt/check, tflint, static security scanner, Conftest with a curated policy bundle, and a dry-run terraform plan using a cached state sandbox. 2) Fail early on policy violations and surface Conftest output as PR review comments. 3) Add plan parsing step that produces a concise human-readable summary (resources to be created/changed/destroyed) and post as a comment with path-level diffs. 4) Optionally gate merges for modules with sensitive resources (KMS, peering, routing) requiring an approval label. 5) Add a lightweight health precheck job that, for staging-only applies, verifies connectivity to critical VPC endpoints and validates expected IAM roles exist.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Deploy reusable GitHub Action templates in infra-ci repo and enable on two module repos (networking and kms). Phase 2: Integrate PR comment annotations and required status checks for module repos. Phase 3: Migrate remaining module repos and add optional integration with Atlantis/Spacelift for controlled apply. Phase 4: Add automated canary apply workflow for major upgrades with rollback hooks.
tasks: Create GitHub Action job templates for preflight steps (fmt, lint, conftest, plan)
Assemble Conftest policy bundle for private deployments and publish to policy-repo
Implement plan-parser that summarizes terraform plan and extracts resource counts
Wire PR comment integration for Conftest and plan-summary (use GitHub Checks API)
Add label-based gating for sensitive-module merges
Implement staging preflight apply job that runs in ephemeral workspace using isolated creds
Document the pipeline and onboarding steps for module owners
Run pilot on 'networking-modules' and 'kms-modules' repos and collect metrics
acceptance_criteria: Preflight action runs on every PR to selected module repos and completes within target time (<= 8 minutes for lint + policy + plan summary)
Conftest policy violations block merge and post readable comments with remediation guidance
Plan summary comment accurately reflects resource creates/updates/destroys and links to module file locations
Staging preflight apply can be executed by CI account and runs health checks against a staging VPC without manual intervention
Documentation exists and at least two module owners have adopted the required status checks
Rollout plan and migration checklist reviewed and approved by platform PM
notes: We intentionally keep the staging apply lightweight: use a minimal set of resources to validate behavior rather than a full environment apply.
Conftest policy set should be conservative initially (block high-risk changes) and loosen over time as false positives are resolved.
We evaluated OPA Gate but chose Conftest for faster integration with our existing CI and simpler rule authoring during pilot.
Long term we may export policy decisions to a central policy evaluation service for other deployment paths.
Performance: if plan execution time exceeds 8 minutes we will move plan-only jobs to a self-hosted runner pool pinned to a larger runner SKU.
blockers: Service account for CI to create ephemeral state backends in staging (security ticket pending)
Conftest rule tuning requires input from security team for KMS and peering checks
